# tebibcloud_load_balancer_listener (Resource)

A port a load balancer accepts traffic on, and the target group it forwards to.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "tebibcloud_load_balancer_listener" "api" {
  load_balancer_id = tebibcloud_load_balancer.web.id
  port             = 8443
  target_group_id  = tebibcloud_load_balancer_target_group.api.id
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `load_balancer_id` (String) Load balancer ID (`lb-...`). Changing it replaces the listener.
- `port` (Number) Port (1-65535), one listener per port. Changing it replaces the listener.

### Optional

- `certificates` (List of String) `https` listeners: certificate IDs (`cert-...`, up to 5, issued), in order. The first is the default; SNI picks the others. Changes in place. With `managed_certificate` it holds the new certificate once it is issued.
- `managed_certificate` (Attributes) `https` listeners, instead of `certificates`: request a free managed certificate for these names (in DNS zones hosted with TebibCloud, validated over DNS) together with the listener. The listener is created at once, has `status` `certificate_pending` and serves nothing until the certificate is issued; then it is attached automatically. Changing it replaces the listener. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--managed_certificate))
- `project_id` (String) Project ID (`p-...`). Default: the provider's `project`. Changing it replaces the resource.
- `protocol` (String) `tcp` (default), `http` or `https`. Changing it replaces the listener. A `tcp` listener needs a `tcp` target group; `http` and `https` listeners an `http` one, or an `https` one (an `https` listener ends TLS here and sends plain HTTP, or TLS again, to the targets).
- `redirect_port` (Number) The port the redirect points at. Default 443.
- `redirect_to_https` (Boolean) `http` listeners: answer every request with a 301 to HTTPS (the Let's Encrypt HTTP-01 path is answered first). Such a listener has no target group.
- `target_group_id` (String) Target group to forward to (`lbtg-...`). Changes in place. Not for a listener with `redirect_to_https`.
- `timeouts` (Block, Optional) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--timeouts))
- `tls_policy` (String) `https` listeners: the TLS policy. Only `tls12-intermediate` (TLS 1.2 and 1.3, the default) exists today. Changing it replaces the listener.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Listener ID (`lbl-...`).
- `pending_certificate_id` (String) The managed certificate the listener waits for (`cert-...`), until it is attached.
- `status` (String) `active`, `certificate_pending` (waiting for the managed certificate), or `no_certificate` for an https listener with nothing to serve.

<a id="nestedatt--managed_certificate"></a>
### Nested Schema for `managed_certificate`

Required:

- `domain_names` (Set of String) Up to 5 names; `*.example.com` wildcards are allowed.

Optional:

- `create_records` (Boolean) Also create the missing `A` records of the names (not wildcards) in their hosted zone, pointing at this load balancer. An existing record is never changed. Default `true`.
- `name` (String) The certificate's name. Default: made from the first name.


<a id="nestedblock--timeouts"></a>
### Nested Schema for `timeouts`

Optional:

- `create` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours).
- `delete` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours). Setting a timeout for a Delete operation is only applicable if changes are saved into state before the destroy operation occurs.
- `update` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours).

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# <load_balancer_id>/<listener_id>, optionally with <project_id>/ in front.
terraform import tebibcloud_load_balancer_listener.api lb-abc123/lbl-def456
```
